channel.title: Vox
channel.description: Updates for Vox — read selected text aloud and dictate, on-device.

item.title: 1.29.0b6
item.description:
Vox 1.29.0b6 (2026-10-24)

No more stuck pill. If a live transcription engine ever freezes while it finishes your dictation, Vox now gives up on its own instead of waiting until you press Esc. Your recording is kept in History, so you can run it again with Transcribe Again.

Vox 1.29.0b5 (2026-10-24)

A timer you can trust. The timer in the listening pill now starts when Vox actually hears you, the moment the waveform comes alive. It no longer counts the second the microphone takes to wake up, or the time a model takes to load. Anything you say while the model loads is still kept.

An easier engine list. In Settings › Listening, the Parakeet engines now sit together, with Fluid Speech Mini at the top and Voz at the bottom.

Vox 1.29.0b4 (2026-10-24)

History is easier to scan. Each dictation now shows a short title from its first words, with its length right beside it, so you can spot that long meeting note at a glance. Click a row to read the whole thing.

Vox 1.29.0b3 (2026-10-23)

Long dictations keep every word. With Fluid Speech Mini, a long dictation or recording could lose a few sentences in the middle. Vox now notices a quiet stretch where you were still talking and listens to it again, so nothing goes missing.

Vox 1.29.0b2 (2026-10-23)

Talk as long as you like. The 5-minute limit is gone. Vox saves your voice to disk while you speak, so a long meeting note or a rambling idea is never lost. If something goes wrong (a crash, a failed transcription, or you press Esc), the recording waits for you in History.

Try again with a different engine. Right-click a dictation in History and choose Transcribe Again to run it through any engine you have downloaded. A progress bar shows how far it is, and your old text stays if you change your mind.

A new engine to try: Parakeet Unified (Beta). Your words appear as you speak, already with punctuation and capitals. The first dictation after you choose it takes a little while to prepare; after that it is quick.

Make the pill yours. In Settings › Listening, choose whether the pill shows your words as you talk, a recording dot, and a timer.

Smaller things you will notice

  • Dictionary search is at the top of the list. Press Cmd+F to jump to it.

Vox 1.28.0 (2026-10-22)

Added

  • Control Center and the Now Playing widget now show a scrubber that seeks the read-aloud (#96).

Changed

  • AGENTS.md has a recipe that tells a TCC-wedged test run from a hung test (#149).

Fixed

  • A superseded read-aloud that waits for the synthesis gate now stops there. It no longer runs a full generate (#96).
  • Quit or a Sparkle relaunch during a muted dictation restores the system volume (#96).
  • After a crash or force quit during a muted dictation, the next launch restores the output mute or volume that Vox changed. A level you changed since then stays (#96).
  • The STT and TTS routers guard the active model ID with a lock, and the @unchecked Sendable router and player types state why they are safe (#96).
  • Removed the unused ModifierReleaseWaiter.wait. The clipboard capture posts modifier key-ups instead (#96).

Vox 1.28.0 (2026-10-22)

Added

  • Control Center and the Now Playing widget now show a scrubber that seeks the read-aloud (#96).

Changed

  • AGENTS.md has a recipe that tells a TCC-wedged test run from a hung test (#149).

Fixed

  • A superseded read-aloud that waits for the synthesis gate now stops there. It no longer runs a full generate (#96).
  • Quit or a Sparkle relaunch during a muted dictation restores the system volume (#96).
  • After a crash or force quit during a muted dictation, the next launch restores the output mute or volume that Vox changed. A level you changed since then stays (#96).
  • The STT and TTS routers guard the active model ID with a lock, and the @unchecked Sendable router and player types state why they are safe (#96).
  • Removed the unused ModifierReleaseWaiter.wait. The clipboard capture posts modifier key-ups instead (#96).

Vox 1.27.1 (2026-10-22)

Changed

  • Update notes now list this version and the four before it, so an update that skips versions shows every change.
  • The dictation done hold takes an injectable clock, so its test no longer depends on wall-clock timing.
  • Tests no longer put a real floating pill or player panel on screen under swift test; one shared check now detects the test host.

Fixed

  • On a Mac where Vox has never asked for the microphone, "Allow…" and the "Vox can't hear you" banner now show the macOS prompt. Before, they opened System Settings, which does not list Vox until Vox has asked.
  • The first dictation press on a Mac where Vox has never asked for the microphone now shows the macOS prompt instead of a notice that points to System Settings. That press does not record; the next press does (#104).
  • The listening waveform no longer pins at full height during normal speech. One dBFS mapping now sets the bar level (speech at -20 dBFS draws about 0.73, room noise stays at the silence floor), and bars rise fast and fall slowly. The window, curve and smoothing are PillTuning knobs in the tuning panel.
  • Dictation keeps recording when you switch the microphone mid-recording (for example when AirPods connect). A new dictation after a switch no longer fails with an audio format error. If Vox cannot continue, it keeps what it heard and shows a "Recording stopped" notice.
  • Streaming dictation no longer drops the last word or two when you stop. Vox now stops the microphone before it closes the stream to the recognizer, so the final audio reaches it, and it feeds one chunk of silence so the last word decodes in full. (#179)
  • Fuzzy dictionary matching no longer turns common words into an entry ("soft" or "sift the" into "Swift") and never swallows the next word. A single heard word needs 5 letters and a close spelling.
  • When two entries sound alike, the closest spelling wins, not the list order.
  • Accented letters count as their plain letters in sound matching.
  • A CSV export and import keeps a trigger that contains "·".
  • A CSV file with no header row keeps its first row, and the Dictionary tab shows how many entries an import added.
  • The Dictionary rejects a spoken form that has no letter or digit.
  • "Mute other audio" now silences output devices that have no master mute (for example USB audio interfaces). Vox tries master mute, per-channel mute, then the volume, restores exactly what it changed, and logs any failure.
  • A synthesis failure after playback started no longer leaves a stuck "Synthesis failed" pill. The played audio ends first, the error pill has a close button, and a retryable error dismisses itself after 8 seconds (#161).
  • Vox now notices a model you deleted outside the app (for example in Finder). The next read-aloud or dictation downloads the model again and shows the download progress, instead of failing at load.
  • Catalog download sizes now match the real download: Kokoro 361 MB (was 164 MB), Parakeet Realtime 450 MB (was 360 MB), Voz 337 MB (was 466 MB). A gated test (VOX_RUN_NETWORK_TESTS=1) checks every figure against the Hugging Face listing (#138).

item.title: 1.29.0b1
item.description:
Vox 1.29.0b1 (2026-10-23)

Added

  • Parakeet Realtime's Stop after silence menu now offers 1.5, 3, 5, 10 and 30 seconds and Never. With Never, a toggle dictation runs until you press the shortcut again, up to the 5-minute cap. A Shortcuts run still stops after 0.75 s of silence.
  • Vox moves models from the pre-1.15.0 ~/Documents/huggingface folder into its own models folder at launch. It never deletes them. A model that already exists there stays untouched, and a failed move shows a notice on the Storage tab (#143).
  • The Storage tab lists the folders that older Vox versions left in ~/Documents/huggingface and ~/.cache/huggingface/hub, and removes them after a confirmation that names each path and the total size (#113).
  • About has an "Export diagnostics" link (#110). It saves one zip with the build, timings, crash records, macOS crash reports, and the last 24 hours of the Vox log. The zip has no transcripts, history, dictionary, or audio. Vox sends nothing.
  • scripts/test.sh runs the SwiftPM tests in one command: build lock, build, Sparkle copy, the real exit code, and the 10 slowest tests. Its watchdog samples a silent run into build/hangs/, names the stuck test, and exits 124 without a kill.

Changed

  • In dark appearance, the listening pill's scrim now follows the Liquid Glass setting: lighter at Clear (0.32), full at Tinted (0.4), and full under Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast. Text stays at 4.5:1 or better.
  • The Pill Tuning Panel preview now drives the shipped pill and opens on a short Text layout section (top inset, gap, bottom inset, line height, font size, max lines) with a Copy values button. Dead knobs and controls are gone.
  • Stale planning documents moved to docs/archive/ with git mv: the 1.19.0 task list, the design-system and SwiftUI audits, the onboarding plan, docs/superpowers/, and the finished audit and handoff files. Links in AGENTS.md, docs/spec/, docs/design/ and scripts/ now point at the new paths. AGENTS.md names the parent session and branch sessions in place of the old coordinator roles.
  • scripts/clean-worktrees.sh no longer removes a worktree that a running session uses. A new session's branch has no commits yet and looked merged into main.
  • scripts/release.sh publish also creates the release on gregbarbosa/Vox, tagged at the shipped commit, so the source repo lists every version.

Fixed

  • The listening pill dims its dot and waveform from the press until the microphone is on, then brightens; the start sound plays at that moment. Some USB interfaces (a Scarlett 2i2) take about 0.6 s to start when no other audio plays through them, and words spoken in that time were lost (#206). Muting other audio now runs during the microphone start, not before it.
  • Settings › Listening says when the output device has no volume control, so "Mute other audio" cannot mute it (#206).
  • Tests no longer write the real clipboard, post a real Cmd+V, or build a real mic engine. RealUserStateGuardTests now bans those default seams in test sources.
  • The mic recorder and the streamed player no longer make AVFAudio's notification thread wait for the main thread on an audio device change.
  • Best clean up no longer drops all its punctuation when Apple Intelligence changes one word (for example "fail" to "failure" or "fifteen" to "15"). Vox keeps the punctuation and capitals and puts back the words you said, where before it inserted the whole dictation raw. Vox still never inserts a word you did not say (#93).
  • Fast clean up no longer doubles punctuation ("you??", "it..") on text from an engine that already punctuates, such as Fluid Speech Mini.
  • The first dictation after a Fluid Speech Mini download no longer waits about 27 s. Vox prepares the model right after the download, and the Listening page shows "Preparing the model…" until it is ready.
  • The test suite no longer hangs in AVFAudio. Dictation tests muted the Mac's real output, and each mute's settings write waited for the main thread through the updater's defaults observer. Tests now use a no-op mute, and the observer no longer blocks the writer.
  • The listening pill's live transcript now has even space: the gap above the text matches the space below the waveform, and the text no longer crowds the waveform at 3 and 4 lines. The text area always fits its lines, so nothing is clipped.
  • The Best cleanup no longer skips ordinary dictation that mentions violence, drugs, or self-harm. It now uses the same permissive Apple Intelligence guardrails as the rewrite styles (#93).
  • Long dictations get the Best cleanup and the rewrite styles in chunks. Before, a rewrite over about 1,000 words timed out and a Best cleanup over about 1,500 words overflowed the model's context window; both inserted the raw text (#93).
  • Each Apple Intelligence request now has a deadline that grows with its length (30 seconds plus 50 ms per estimated token) and keeps its text on expiry, so a stuck model call can no longer hold the pill on "Cleaning up" (#93).
  • The Best cleanup no longer writes ordinary words in capitals ("The SUSPECT shot the VICTIM"); acronyms such as API keep their capitals (#93).
  • The listening pill shows at the dictation press. On the first press after launch it waited 0.6 to 0.8 s for the microphone to start. Words spoken while the transcription model loads now reach the transcript.
  • VoiceOver now names every player control: play, pause and replay, skip back 15 and forward 30 seconds, collapse, close, dismiss, cancel download, and the scrubber with its position. Remaining time is spoken as "33 seconds left" (#92).
  • VoiceOver can open the player card ("Show Player Controls") and stop a dictation ("Stop Dictation") from the pills, which before worked only by click or hover (#92).
  • The menu-bar item says "Vox" and its state, including a missing Accessibility permission, instead of the symbol name (#92).
  • VoiceOver reads the live transcript as one line, not word by word; Storage Delete and Clear buttons and the About project links name their item (#92).
  • Reduce Motion now stops the player's pill-to-card morph, the speed overlay's scale-in, and the transcript's scroll animation (#92).
  • With VoiceOver on, Vox announces when it inserts text, when reading finishes, and when an error happens. It stays silent when recording or reading starts (#92).
  • The menu bar has Skip Back 15 Seconds and Skip Forward 30 Seconds while a clip plays, so keyboard users can skip (#92).
  • The player card's time labels are darker. With Increase Contrast on, the selected playback speed has a ring and the download bar is stronger (#92).

  • The listening pill no longer goes missing on back-to-back dictations. A press within about a second of the text landing used to start recording with no pill on screen, and the next press opened an empty pill. The pill now stays up and springs back when a new dictation starts during its fade.

  • The listening pill no longer goes missing on back-to-back dictations. The pill stays up and springs back when a new dictation starts during its fade.

  • Imported dictionary entries now work.

  • Beta updates. Settings > General > Software Update has a new setting, "Get beta updates". It is off by default. Turn it on to get early versions of Vox before they are released to all users. A beta can be less stable.

What's new

  • The dictation pill grows one line at a time. It starts at the height of one text line and grows by one line when a word wraps, up to 4 lines. Then the text scrolls. Words on screen do not move.
  • Words end solid. Each new word fades in, then shows in the same color as the other words. The last word no longer stays grey.
  • Better contrast in Dark Mode. The pill text now passes 4.5:1 contrast on a light backdrop.
  • Fixed: the waveform no longer draws under the button at the right end of the pill. The button is easier to click.

  • Fixed: the playback-speed picker in the floating player. It no longer detaches from the card, floats off the player, or closes after a few taps — it now stays anchored, dismisses on outside tap, and reads clearly on its own surface.
  • Kokoro 82M (Neural Engine) audio parity: loudness now matches the default MLX engine (measured ±0.05 dB) and the low-frequency rumble/DC artifact at chunk joins is gone.
  • Under the hood: a full root-cause investigation of the Neural Engine's residual tonal character (documented in the repo), agent-tooling and window-capture improvements for design review, and Swift 6 language-mode cleanups.

What's new

  • Kokoro 82M (Neural Engine) — new TTS engine (opt-in) — the same Kokoro voices through a 7-stage Core ML pipeline running entirely on the Apple Neural Engine: 19–22.6× realtime, 75–850 ms time-to-first-chunk, stable under heavy system load. English launch set (28 voices, US + UK); ~95 MB download; native generation-speed knob. Pick it in Settings → Voice → Engine, right under “Kokoro 82M” — the default engine is unchanged.
  • Faster Kokoro on the default engine — the GPU vectorization pass drops warm synthesis to 5–8× faster than before, approaching heart-nano speed at heart quality.
  • Fixed a cache bug that re-downloaded 9 MB of phonemizer data on every model load for fresh installs (both engines benefit).

What's new

  • Voz speech-recognition engine (opt-in) — on-device transcription on the Apple Neural Engine: ~5× faster on long dictations than the MLX default, at a 466 MB download (vs 2.3 GB), with matching accuracy. Pick it in Settings → Listening → Engine; the default engine is unchanged.
  • Voz is powered by Desert Ant Labs and credited in Settings → About.

Honest sizes for the speech-recognition model

  • The Storage tab shows the speech-recognition model as one row with the total size of every latency setting you downloaded. The row expands to show each setting with its own size and its own Delete button.
  • The row now tells you the truth about disk space. It used to report the size of every latency setting but delete only the one you use, so you got back about a third of the space Vox named. Each row now frees exactly the space it names.

Vox gives you your disk space back

  • Vox reclaims space that earlier versions left behind. When Vox starts, it removes duplicate copies of models that no loader reads. On a Mac that used earlier versions this can free hundreds of megabytes. Vox never removes a model you use.
  • Deleting a model now removes every copy of it. Before this, Vox kept two cached copies, so you got back about one third of the space Vox told you it freed.

More control in the Storage tab

  • Clear your recordings, your voice previews, and partial downloads. Vox asks you to confirm before it removes recordings, because Vox cannot recreate them. The text stays in History.
  • Every row has a Reveal in Finder button.
  • The Listening tab lists the speech models you downloaded, with the real size of each one and a Remove button.

Vox downloads the voice for you

  • The first time you use a voice that is not on your Mac yet, Vox downloads it and shows you the download. Before this, Vox refused to speak and the hotkey did nothing on a new install.
  • The download appears in the floating pill with the voice name, a progress bar, and the time remaining. Vox shows the time only when it can measure it.
  • The pill has a cancel button. Cancel stops the transfer and removes what it already downloaded.

See and manage what Vox stores

  • Settings has a Storage tab. It lists every file Vox stores, with the real size on disk and a total.
  • You can delete a model. Vox asks you to confirm, and names the model and the space you get back. If you delete the voice you use now, Vox tells you it must download that voice again.
  • Vox no longer downloads model files it cannot use. Every model you download from now on costs what it should.

Do more with what you just said

Everything Vox has spoken or heard now sits one click away in the menu bar, and every entry knows what it is. Open Recent and each row carries its own actions: play it back, copy it, or drop it straight into whatever app you are working in.

  • Actions on every recent entry — Play, Copy, and Insert at Cursor
  • Your own voice, played back — a dictation replays the recording Vox made, instead of reading your words back in a synthetic voice
  • Instant replay — playing something again uses the recording Vox already has, with no model to load and no waiting
  • See what each entry is — a speaker icon for what Vox spoke, a microphone for what Vox heard
  • Fixed — the floating player no longer opens clipped below the bottom of the screen

✨ The Liquid Glass listening experience

Vox's dictation pill is reborn in Liquid Glass. Speak, and your words rise through a live teleprompter inside a single living pane of glass — the top line softly fading as new lines flow in. Stop, and the whole pill folds down in one continuous, glass-smooth motion: your text holds for a beat, then gracefully dissolves as the pill settles. No seams, no jumps — one fluid gesture, rendered entirely on-device.

  • Live teleprompter that scrolls naturally as you dictate
  • One seamless collapse — no flicker, no snap
  • A fuller, livelier waveform while you speak
  • Refined Listening settings — Toggle Dictation now leads

Beautiful, fast, and 100% on your Mac.

Redesigned dictation pill

  • The recording pill now morphs as you dictate — growing to show your live transcript alongside a scrolling waveform, then settling back to a compact capsule when you're done.
  • It now renders in Liquid Glass that adapts to your system appearance, matching the playback mini-player.

Fixes

  • Spoken audio now shows the correct play/pause state and accurate elapsed time in Control Center.

Improvements

  • Under-the-hood build and reliability improvements. No changes to how Vox works day to day.

New

  • Rewrite styles for dictation. Just talk — Vox now cleans up what you said. It drops filler words (“um”, “you know”), tidies false starts, and applies your self-corrections (“Tuesday — no, Wednesday” becomes “Wednesday”). Pick how it shapes the result: Clean to just neaten it up, or Email, Message, Notes, and Prose to format for where it’s going — or keep Verbatim (the default) for exactly what you said. It runs on-device with Apple Intelligence, so nothing leaves your Mac. Choose a style in Settings → Listening, or from the new wand button on the recording pill.

New

  • User Dictionary. Teach Vox your names, jargon, and spoken shortcuts. The new Dictionary tab in Settings lets you add words and replacements with a live preview — say “my work email” and the address lands in your text; technical terms come out spelled and capitalized right, on every accuracy setting. Sounds-alike matching fixes common mishearings automatically, and your dictionary imports/exports as CSV or JSON.

Fixed

  • No more repeated update prompts. If Vox kept offering you the same update after installing it, this release cures it for good.
  • Internal test-reliability fixes that make every future release better-verified.

New

  • Drive Vox from Shortcuts and Siri. The “Speak Selection” and “Speak Text” actions now work reliably — no more “Shortcuts couldn’t communicate with the app.” Vox runs the action in the background, so the app you’re working in keeps focus.
  • New “Listen and Transcribe” action. Start dictation from a Shortcut: Vox records, transcribes on-device, and hands the text back to the Shortcut so you can pipe it anywhere — notes, messages, automations. It stops automatically when you stop talking.

Fixed

  • A broken speech-model download no longer sticks dictation at “Model not ready.” Vox now detects an incomplete model on disk, cleans it up, and re-downloads it automatically — and a Download button appears on the model card so you’re never stuck.
  • Switching the Listening latency tier is smoother. The new tier loads immediately after switching, and previously downloaded tiers stay cached so switching back is instant.
  • Clearer error messages when a Shortcut can’t run (model still downloading, microphone permission needed).

New

  • Long passages now read all the way through. Selections that used to fail with “Synthesis failed” are split into natural chunks and start playing while the rest is still being prepared, so audio begins almost immediately.

Fixed

  • Reading aloud in Safari no longer disturbs your clipboard. Vox now captures your Safari selection directly, even on the very first try, instead of falling back to copy-and-paste.
  • Closing the player mid-synthesis makes it stay closed. The floating player no longer pops back open (or shows a raw model name) when you dismiss it while a long passage is still being prepared.
  • A calmer launch. Vox no longer force-opens System Settings on startup — it shows a gentle menu-bar prompt and only opens Settings when you ask to grant access.

Fixed

  • Crash on rapid hotkey presses. Pressing the speak hotkey again while Vox was still working could crash the app. A new press now cleanly interrupts and replaces the one in progress.
  • More reliable text capture. Selected-text capture is more robust in browsers and other apps, with a smarter clipboard fallback that no longer reads stale or unrelated clipboard content when nothing is selected.

Improved

  • Faster, more accurate transcript cleanup. The Fast “Clean up transcript” tier downloads and runs an on-device punctuation model on first use, with an instant rule-based fallback so it never blocks.
  • Dictation download progress. The Parakeet dictation model now shows a real progress bar with a working Cancel button in Settings → Listening.
  • Capture diagnostics. Settings → Debug now shows exactly why a capture succeeded or failed (per-strategy results and timings).
  • AirPods audio quality. Opening Settings no longer holds the microphone open, so Bluetooth output stays at full quality.

Fixed

  • Microphone permission on macOS. Dictation can now request microphone access — the system permission prompt appears and the grant registers correctly. (Previously no prompt ever showed and access was stuck off.)
